key_insight: A first-principles nonequilibrium Bethe-Salpeter plus molecular-dynamics framework separates electronic from lattice effects in transient absorption of CH3NH3PbBr3, showing electronic screening dominates femtosecond dynamics while thermal lattice effects govern picosecond behavior.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more reliable way to interpret pump-probe and X-ray/optical transient spectra in perovskites, helping engineers distinguish carrier physics from lattice heating in device diagnostics.
method: Nonequilibrium Bethe-Salpeter equation for excited-state spectra
Ab initio molecular dynamics for thermal lattice motion
Time-resolved decomposition of electronic vs lattice contributions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative agreement across femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales and identifies distinct dominant mechanisms in X-ray and optical transient absorption.
watch_item: The approach is computationally intensive and system-specific, so extending it to larger device-scale materials sets may require substantial cost and careful validation.
paper_title: Disentangling Electronic and Lattice Contributions to Transient Absorption in Metal Halide Perovskites: A First-Principles Study of CH3NH3PbBr3
